findings.description: FIND — resume mode cannot reliably resume the latest run because `_find_or_create_logs_dir()` looks for `checkpoint.json`, while this runner persists its own state to `runner_state.json` and later resume logic reads `runner_state.json` plus `brain.load_checkpoint()`. Premises: (1) `_find_or_create_logs_dir()` under `if cfg.resume:` returns the first log dir where `(c / "checkpoint.json").exists()`. (2) This file writes runner state to `runner_state.json` every round. (3) HIL pause path calls `brain._save_checkpoint()`, which may create `checkpoint.json`, but ordinary runs and crashes between `brain.persist()`/runner-state writes are only guaranteed to have `runner_state.json`. Concrete trace: create `bench/logs/ref_x_20260413T000000Z/runner_state.json` with valid registry state, but no `checkpoint.json`; start with `--resume`. `_find_or_create_logs_dir()` finds no matching checkpoint, creates a fresh timestamped directory, then `brain.load_checkpoint()` runs in the new directory and resume silently starts from round 0. Expected: resume should pick the existing run with persisted state. Actual: it can fork a new run and lose continuity. Formal conclusion: the resume directory selector is keyed to the wrong checkpoint artifact and can silently break resumability, which is a high-severity correctness fault in a long-running experiment runner.

    if cfg.resume:

        candidates = sorted(

            key=lambda p: p.name, reverse=True,

        for c in candidates:
            if (c / "checkpoint.json").exists():

Premises: (1) `consecutive_churn_rounds` increments whenever `_compute_rho(...).churn` is true. Concrete trace: last phase ends with `consecutive_churn_rounds = 3` and `gamma >= 0.45`; integration starts; histories are empty but churn counter remains 3. Expected: integration should start with fresh convergence state. Actual: stale churn state leaks across phases. Formal conclusion: this is a confirmed state-leak bug that can cause premature integration termination.

findings.description: FIND — `run_experiment()` computes cumulative context telemetry from response lengths instead of prompt/context lengths, so endocrine context-budget monitoring is measuring output volume, not actual context pressure. Premises: (1) The code comment says “Each model's budget adapts to its measured prompt performance.” (2) `prompt_lengths` is already computed in `_dispatch_round_star/_dispatch_round_relay` as `len(prompt) + len(cdsfl_text)`. Expected endocrine pacing should detect heavy prompt pressure. Actual telemetry underreports by ~40x and can suppress pacing/health signals. Formal conclusion: this is a confirmed correctness bug in the monitoring path; it silently corrupts the control signal used for pacing.

findings.description: FIND — HIL review in burst mode can re-pause forever at the same phase boundary because the pause path exits before marking any “already paused/reviewed” progress in `burst_state`, and the resume path restores `burst_state` unchanged. Premises: (1) In burst convergence handling, when `cfg.hil_review` is true, the code writes a partial report and `sys.exit(42)` before advancing `phase_idx`, `integration_started`, `phase_round_offset`, or resetting convergence state. (2) `runner_state.json` persists `burst_state`. (3) On resume, `_restored_burst` is loaded verbatim. (4) The same round/phase convergence condition remains true, so execution re-enters the same HIL gate and exits 42 again. Concrete trace: phase 0 converges; burst HIL gate writes report and exits. Resume restores `burst_state["phase_idx"] == 0`, current registry/histories still at converged boundary, then re-executes the same branch and exits again before transition to phase 1. findings.description: FIND — `_dispatch_round_star()` and `_dispatch_round_relay()` advertise a 3-tuple return type but actually return 4 values, creating a wrong interface contract that can cause unpacking failures or unsafe reuse. Premises: (1) Both function signatures annotate `-> Tuple[List[Finding], Dict[str, str], Dict[str, float]]`. (2) Both return `findings, responses, per_model_durations, prompt_lengths`. Concrete trace: any future caller using the annotation or following the signature will write `a, b, c = _dispatch_round_star(...)` and raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack`. Static tooling will also infer the wrong API. Expected: signature and implementation match. Actual: public helper contract is inconsistent. Formal conclusion: confirmed interface bug; medium severity but trivial to fix.

findings.description: FIND — burst-mode phase transitions clear the global novelty/raw/gamma/rho histories in place, but final reporting uses those same lists as experiment-wide histories. Premises: (1) on each phase transition in `run_experiment()`, the code executes `gate_history.clear(); stall_history.clear(); novelty_counts.clear(); raw_counts.clear(); rho_history.clear(); gamma_history.clear(); open_ch_history.clear()`; (2) at finalisation it emits `result["gamma_history"] = [round(g, 4) for g in gamma_history]`; (3) it also writes `novelty_counts`, `raw_counts`, `rho_history`, and `gamma_history` into checkpoints as if they were persistent run state. Expected: final report/checkpoint should preserve experiment-wide telemetry, while phase-local convergence windows may reset separately. Actual: one set of lists is used for both incompatible purposes. findings.description: FIND — CLI validation checks `args.pattern` even when configuration is loaded from JSON, so `--config` cannot supply a non-default pattern unless the caller redundantly passes the same CLI flag. Premises: (1) when `--config` is provided, `cfg = RunnerConfig.from_json(args.config)` may set `cfg.pattern`; (2) later validation is `if args.pattern not in INTERACTION_PATTERN_PRESETS:` rather than `cfg.pattern`; (3) argparse gives `args.pattern` its default `"fff"` unless explicitly passed. Expected: config-driven pattern `"xyz"` is accepted. Actual: validation inspects `args.pattern == "fff"` and the run proceeds using `cfg.pattern == "xyz"` without validating it; conversely, if config contained invalid `"bad"` and CLI omitted `--pattern`, the invalid config escapes validation entirely. Actual: later burst-mode branches depend on `burst_plan` and `burst_state` coherence but only `burst_state` is restored. FIND — `_itc_adapt()` hardcodes `"findings": 0` in every history entry (line ~in the `state["history"].append(...)` call), regardless of the actual findings count produced by the model. This corrupts the ITC escalation logic in `_itc_detect()`, which reads `h.get("findings") == 0` from recent history to decide between TRANSIENT_FAILURE and CAPABILITY_MISMATCH. Scenario: a model produces 5 findings but triggers DEGRADATION (low parse yield) → history records `"findings": 0`. Next round, model produces 0 actual findings → `_itc_detect` sees the prior `"findings": 0` entry → `recent_empty >= 1` → returns CAPABILITY_MISMATCH instead of TRANSIENT_FAILURE. This causes premature escalation (strip_context or section_assign instead of retry), silently degrading model output quality when a simple retry would have sufficed.

findings.description: FIND — `_resolve_merge_source()` fails to resolve F-prefix finding IDs from MERGE verdicts. The `contested_count()` and `open_crit_high_count()` are also inflated, potentially blocking the convergence gate.
